new_value: free slots ranked by per-rank DPS (total_raw / effective cooldown) - consistent across the matrix

evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

sources_quoted.where: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 1.1 (Renewal theory for cast + auto timing schedules)
sources_quoted.quote: Theorem (renewal-reward). For a renewal process with interarrival times X_i and i.i.d. rewards R_i attached to each cycle, the long-run average reward rate is E[R]/E[X] ... The expected-damage-per-second of a rotation is the reward rate E[cycle damage]/E[cycle time]; every sustained fight number in the engine is this finite-horizon renewal-reward functional.
sources_quoted.bears_on: Justifies the metric itself: for a single ability considered alone the cycle is one cast, so E[R]/E[X] = total_raw / effective_cooldown exactly. The proposed ranking key is not an ad-hoc heuristic, it is the engine's own reward rate restricted to one ability.

sources_quoted.quote: the cast epochs of a solo ability are 0, c_i, 2c_i, ... - again a deterministic renewal schedule; the shared-timeline version is the superposition with mutual-exclusion, resolved greedily by cast order.
sources_quoted.bears_on: Confirms a cast-order priority exists and is the tie-break for the mutual-exclusion greedy schedule, i.e. there is a well-defined thing for 'free slots ranked by ...' to determine.

sources_quoted.where: docs/math-foundations.md, Section 5 formula-audit table, ability-haste row
sources_quoted.quote: | Ability haste (`effective_cooldown`) | `cd' = cd*100/(100+AH)`; casts/unit time affine in AH | EXACT | R casts exactly once per timed fight (model constraint, documented) |
sources_quoted.bears_on: Supplies the effective-cooldown denominator used below, and establishes that R occupies a forced/single slot rather than competing for free slots - so R's position in the DPS ranking is inert.

sources_quoted.where: data/champions.json -> Syndra.abilities.R, first effect description (cached wiki text)

sources_quoted.bears_on: Independent proof from the cache that Dark Sphere's cooldown IS a haste-responsive quantity - so the `affectedByCdr: false` flag on Q is a data-model artifact of the rechargeRate/charge representation, not a claim that haste does not apply to Q. independent_computation.formula: per_rank_DPS(ability) = total_raw(rank, AP) / effective_cooldown(rank, AH),  effective_cooldown = base_cd * 100/(100+AH)   [S1, S3]
independent_computation.rank_set: Level 18 derived order gives Q5 / W5 / E5 / R3 (5+5+5+3 = 18 skill points), i.e. the free slots after the three forced R slots at levels 6/11/16.

worked_example_AH_0_AP_0.order: Q > W > E > R (R_max edges E only in the degenerate AP=0, all-7-spheres reading)

worked_example_AH_120_AP_200.note: all four cooldowns scale by the same factor 100/220 = 0.4545, so the ranking is scale-invariant

matrix_swept.result: Q > W > E > R in all 16 cells (using the R minimum / 3-sphere reading, which is the only one that describes a cast with no pre-placed spheres). The single exception anywhere in the sweep is R_max slipping above E at AP=0 exactly, which is a corner of the sweep with no AP and a full 7-sphere board, and it does not touch the free-slot order because R is a forced slot [S3].

independent_computation.free_slot_order_derived: Q first, then W, then E (R never competes: forced at 6/11/16 and 'R casts exactly once per timed fight' [S3]).
independent_computation.external_sanity_check: That derivation reproduces the real-game Syndra max order (Q max first, W second, E last, R on cooldown) - an independent confirmation that the metric picks the right ability, not just a self-consistent one.
independent_computation.on_the_leaf_appearing: sources[7] going from absent to present means the derived-order rotation list is one entry longer than the previous fixed list. Nothing in the cached data or in docs/math-foundations.md contradicts an eighth entry: the shared-timeline greedy schedule [S2] with Q5/W5/E5/R3 cooldowns (7 / 8 / 15 / 80 s before haste) plus the 0.25 s sourced cast times produces the cast sequence Q, W, E, R, Q, W, Q, E ... - an eighth cast exists at every haste level in the matrix, so the slot is real rather than a padding artifact.

caveat_flagged.issue: Haste-invariance of the ranking depends on Q being treated as ability-haste affected.
caveat_flagged.detail: data/champions.json marks Syndra Q `cooldown.affectedByCdr: false` (it is stored as a rechargeRate ability). If an implementation honors that flag literally, Q's per-rank DPS is frozen at 230/7 = 32.86 while W's grows linearly in AH, and W overtakes Q at AH = 23.5 (AP=0), 18.5 (AP=100), 15.5 (AP=200), 12.3 (AP=400). Under that reading the order at the '120' cell of the matrix would be W > Q > E > R, and the change note's claim of being 'consistent across the matrix' would be false.
caveat_flagged.resolution: The cache itself refutes the literal reading: Syndra's R passive is stated as 'Dark Sphere's cooldown is reduced equivalent to an amount of ability haste' [S5]. A cooldown that ability haste demonstrably reduces is haste-affected; the flag is describing the charge/recharge representation, not haste immunity. With Q haste-affected, all four denominators carry the same 100/(100+AH) factor, the ratios are haste-invariant, and 'consistent across the matrix' holds exactly as claimed.
caveat_flagged.action_for_owner: Confirm the engine applies ability haste to Syndra Q's recharge. If it does not, this leaf is still correct at AH=0 but the 'consistent across the matrix' justification is not, and the derived order at high-haste cells would be wrong (W-first).

verdict_reasoning: The ranking key is the engine's own renewal-reward rate specialized to one ability [S1], so it is principled rather than ad hoc. Computed independently from the cached wiki numbers [S4], it yields Q > W > E > R in every cell of a 4x4 haste x AP sweep, which reproduces Syndra's real max order and leaves R inert because R holds forced slots [S3]. The eighth rotation slot is supported by the shared-timeline schedule [S2] at every haste level tested. No cached datum contradicts the new value; the one way it could fail (literal reading of Q's affectedByCdr flag) is itself contradicted by the cached R passive text [S5].
